entry: [[Flowering plant]] of the family [[Cucurbitaceae]], grown worldwide for its large, juicy fruit. The species, *Citrullus lanatus*, is a scrambling, trailing [[Vine|vine]] whose fruit is a large berry with a firm rind, botanically termed a *pepo*. The flesh, usually deep red to pink, contains many seeds. The fruit is eaten raw or made into juice or wine, and the rind is edible when pickled or cooked. The modern watermelon originated in Sudan, where it was first domesticated, and watermelons were cultivated in Egypt by 2000 BCE. Dessert varieties spread around the Mediterranean during Roman antiquity. Breeding has produced disease-resistant and seedless varieties, and in 2024 China produced 60% of the world's watermelons.

Triangular tool, a portable [[Inclined plane|inclined plane]], and one of the six [[Simple machine|simple machines]]. It separates two objects or portions of an object, lifts an object, or holds an object in place. It converts a force applied to its blunt end into forces perpendicular to its inclined surfaces. Its mechanical advantage is given by 1/tan α, where α is the tip angle. Wedges have existed for thousands of years; perhaps the first example is the [[Hand axe|hand axe]], made by chipping stone, generally [[Flint|flint]], to form a wedge-shaped edge. In [[Ancient Egypt|ancient Egyptian]] quarries, bronze wedges broke away blocks of stone, and wooden wedges that swelled when soaked with water were also used. A narrow wedge with a long taper, called a gib, finely adjusts the distance between objects in machine tools.

Distilled [[Alcoholic beverage|alcoholic beverage]] made from fermented mash of [[Grain|grains]]. Grains such as [[Barley|barley]], corn, rye, and wheat are used, some of them malted, and the spirit is commonly aged in casks of charred white oak. Production involves fermentation, [[Distillation|distillation]], and aging, and the spirit is strictly regulated in many countries. The word derives from the Gaelic *uisce beatha*, meaning "water of life." The spelling whiskey is common in Ireland and the United States, while whisky is used elsewhere. [[Scotch whisky]] must be distilled and matured in oak casks in Scotland for at least three years. Varieties range from single malt, made from malted barley at one distillery, to blended whiskies that mix malt and grain whiskies.

Free online [[Encyclopedia|encyclopedia]] written and maintained by volunteer editors through open collaboration, using [[Wiki|wiki]] software called MediaWiki. Founded by [[Jimmy Wales]] and [[Larry Sanger]] in 2001, it began as a complementary project to Nupedia, an encyclopedia whose articles were written by experts. It has been hosted since 2003 by the Wikimedia Foundation, an American nonprofit funded mainly by reader donations. The English edition is the largest, with over 7 million articles, and the encyclopedia is available in over 300 languages. Its "neutral point of view" policy arose within its first year. It has been praised for its open structure and broad coverage, and its reliability, criticized in the 2000s, has received greater praise since the late 2010s. Critics cite systemic bias, including gender bias against women and geographical bias against the Global South, and some national governments have censored it.

Iraqi-born British architect, artist, and designer. Hadid studied mathematics at the [[American University of Beirut]] before moving to [[London]] in 1972 to study at the Architectural Association School of Architecture, where she studied with [[Rem Koolhaas]]. Influenced by [[Suprematism]], she adopted painting as a design tool and abstraction as a method, and [[The Guardian]] called her the "Queen of Curves." Her major works include the London Aquatics Centre for the 2012 Olympics, Rome's MAXXI Museum, and the Guangzhou Opera House. She was the first woman to receive the [[Pritzker Architecture Prize]], in 2004, and was made a dame by [[Elizabeth II]] in 2012 for services to architecture. Several buildings, including the Daxing International Airport in [[Beijing]], were still under construction at her death.

Chinese general and first king and emperor of [[Nanyue]]. He served the [[Qin dynasty]] in its conquest of the [[Baiyue]] peoples of [[Guangdong]], [[Guangxi]], and northern [[Vietnam]]. After the Qin fell, he established an independent kingdom centered on Panyu (now [[Guangzhou]]) in 204 BC, and in 185 BC he declared himself emperor. Some Vietnamese historians regard him as the founder of the Triệu dynasty, while some historians contest that he was a foreign invader because of his Han Chinese origin.
